title: Audit stream envelope, compact change representation, and actor identity hashing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: define a streaming-friendly audit event envelope and compact field-change encoding for RBAC v2 admin actions, with a privacy-preserving actor identity hashing strategy that supports SSO/SAML-linked principals and key rotation. The outcome should be: (1) a single event envelope shape that works for real-time streams and batch storage, (2) a compact change representation optimized for small diffs (role grants, permission toggles, policy edits), (3) clear guidance for what to include in actor and target fields to support forensic queries while minimizing PII exposure, and (4) an actor hashing scheme that is reproducible across services, supports salt/version rotation, and allows reversible linking under controlled conditions (for legal/compliance support).

Problem/background: current audit logs are inconsistent across services; admin actions produce large, noisy payloads with full resource snapshots. This makes downstream storage and lookup expensive and increases risk of leaking SSO/PII. RBAC v2 introduces richer privilege objects (role templates, dynamic grants, resource patterns) which change shapes frequently. We need an event contract that supports long-term analysis, fine-grained rollbacks, and cross-service correlation (e.g., correlate a token-auth service event with console admin UI event).

Non-goals: replacing existing retention policies, building the full lookup/indexing service, or designing the storage tier. This ticket focuses on schema, encoding, hash strategy, and rollout plan for instrumenting server components and gateway proxies.
schema_examples: Compact diff examples: field-level operations encoded as small tuples: ["A","/grants/0","principal:team-eng"] => add grant; ["M","/policy/expr","policy:expr:v2-compressed"] => modify; ["D","/grants/3"] => delete. Storing these as arrays reduces event size compared to full object diffs.

Actor identity hashing guidance (string): compute a service-specific HMAC over the canonical principal id (SSO subject or internal service-id) using the cluster key: HMAC_SHA256(cluster_key_v{n}, canonical_principal) => base64; prepend "hmac:v{n}:". Keep mapping table for reversible linkage in a secure vault (KMS-wrapped) and log the key-version in the event for traceability. Do not store raw email or subject in the live event payload.
acceptance_criteria: Schema doc PR merged describing the envelope with field definitions and semantic versioning rules (v1.0) and migration notes.
Compact diff encoding spec added to repo and validated with unit tests covering add/modify/delete ops and nested-list index semantics.
Actor hashing library implemented (Go + TypeScript) with key-rotation support and integration tests demonstrating same hash computed by console and token-service using shared cluster key.
Privacy review completed and signed off by Security including guidance for reversible linkage access control and retention limits.
Benchmarked average serialized event size reduced >=30% compared to current snapshots for typical role-change events (measured on staging).
decision_notes: 2026-02-26 - Decided to use compact array-based ops (A/M/D) instead of JSON Patch to keep wire-size minimal and simple to parse in high-throughput streaming gateways.

2026-02-28 - Agreed on HMAC-based actor hashing with explicit key-version prefix to allow safe rotation without breaking historical attribution. Reversible mapping kept in a vault with strict ACLs (only Security + Compliance can request).
2026-03-01 - Chose to include an optional "rbac_snapshot_ref" pointer in meta for heavy edits to allow offline rehydration while keeping event payloads modest.
implementation_notes: Instrument console, admin-api, and token-service (first wave) to emit the new envelope. Gateway and ingestion pipeline must accept both v0 (legacy) and v1 events during migration.

Provide lightweight SDKs: go/redwood-audit v0.1 and js/redwood-audit v0.1 with helper to compute actor hash and to encode diffs. SDKs expose a switch to attach plain subject for environments with explicit consent.
Add feature-flagged rollout: default to 'hash-only' actor field; enable 'subject-in-clear' in staging only when auditing tests.
risks: If cluster key compromise occurs, ability to link actor hashes to identities could be exposed; mitigation: use per-region keys, KMS rotation, and emergency revocation policy.
Partial adoption across services may complicate cross-service joins; plan to backfill important events from older services during migration window.
Some downstream analytics consumers may expect full resource snapshots; need to coordinate with data-platform to provide rehydration paths using rbac_snapshot_ref.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement SDK + schema PR + unit tests; begin instrumentation on console and admin-api behind feature flags.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): instrument token-service and ingress gateway; run end-to-end functional tests and privacy review.
Phase 3 (4 weeks): enable production emit for core services, monitor event sizes and queryability; run backfill job for critical role-change events.
Post-rollout: deprecate legacy snapshot-heavy events after 90 days with announcement and migration docs.
next_steps: Create schema PR with examples and versioning guidance (owner: Diego).
Implement minimal actor-hash library and publish to internal package registry (owner: Diego).
Schedule privacy review with Security (owner: Maya).
Identify top 5 downstream consumers and document rehydration contract (owner: Data Platform liaison).
